## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

All supplemental arms used the same tested commit/tree as the main record, on the same disposable FreeIPA 4.13.4 (AlmaLinux 9.8) server and Ubuntu 24.04 clients. The main chain starts from an enrolled realm without a gateway ledger or fixture marker. The three-node recovery arms restore an enrolled baseline between cases; no production inventory or host was used.

| Arm | Actual result |
|---|---|
| Direct absent host outside the current client inventory | The explicit FQDN/alias retirement authorization permits cleanup. The host is deleted, the other member remains, and the shared hostgroup, HBAC and sudo immutable IDs/targets are preserved. Real survivor SSH/sudo returns `pilotuser` and UID `0`. |
| Missing exact retirement mapping with narrowed task selection | The actual generated inventory contains only the authority and survivor; the absent roster host has no retirement tuple. A `users`-tag reconcile exits 2 at the early always-selected preflight with exact alias/FQDN/stage and recovery guidance. No user-deletion task runs; native object snapshots and ledger are unchanged, the retiring client remains enrolled, and survivor SSH/sudo succeeds. |
| Unknown prefix-matching group | Formal plan exits 1 and direct reconcile exits 2 with `unproven hostgroup ownership` and exact-ID adoption/owning-controller guidance. Object snapshots and ledger are unchanged; the retiring client remains enrolled; survivor SSH/sudo succeeds. |
| Hostgroup deleted and recreated with the same name | Formal plan exits 1 and direct reconcile exits 2. The replacement is not adopted implicitly; its fixture state, ledger and client enrollment are unchanged. The fixture deliberately removes the old authorization target, so this arm makes no survivor-access claim. |
| Automember rule deleted and recreated with the same name | Formal plan exits 1 and direct reconcile exits 2 on unproven automember ownership. Native object snapshots and ledger remain unchanged; client enrollment and survivor SSH/sudo are preserved. LDAP multivalue ordering is normalized while request identity, cardinality and raw captures are retained. |
| Partial failure at the existing service-principal deletion gate | A test HTTP principal intentionally blocks deletion after scope detachment: rc 2, ok=69, changed=1, failed=1. The host remains, the survivor retains SSH/sudo, and a native automember rebuild does not re-add the retiring host. Removing only that test service allows retry: rc 0, ok=84, changed=3, failed=0; another reconcile gives ok=78, changed=0, failed=0. |
| Stale publishers and native automember | Deleted mapped aliases, native short names, administrative recreation of the retired FQDN, native rebuild, stale explicit-FQDN reconcile, disable/re-enable-auto and publication of a new automatic scope all succeed without admitting the retired FQDN. Original group/HBAC/sudo IDs and targets remain intact; the new group contains only the survivor. |
| Disable-auto with stale inherited host input | An inventory group variable names a nonexistent host. Disable succeeds, the owned rule is absent, and the group UUID/members remain unchanged. Re-enable followed by native rebuild still excludes the retired FQDN. |
| Canonical authority and explicit override | The complete main and supplemental CLI flows use `freeipa_server_fqdn` without an input `ipa_server_fqdn`. A separate native publisher run with an explicit one-shot alias override succeeds and preserves group/rule identities and membership. |
| Formal CLI decommission and resume | Plan is executable for the exact inventory alias/FQDN. Apply exits 0 with status `completed` and `Verified=true`; only the retiring host is removed from inventory. Native host deletion, shared group/rule preservation and survivor SSH/sudo pass. Resume exits 0 with `already_completed` and retains the verified completed receipt. |

The original residual-membership failure was reproduced on the pre-fix base with rc 2, changed=0, failed=1. The final main chain and supplemental results above are from the tested candidate, not that baseline. Raw command outputs, native API snapshots, source/input fingerprints and failed development attempts remain in controlled local acceptance storage; this committed record is the standalone sanitized summary required by the repository's retention contract.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- This is day-2 lifecycle evidence on an enrolled single-authority realm, not a fresh full-site installation or multi-authority/replica failover test. Native server/client versions and image hashes are bound above.
- Native partial recovery is a late service-gate failure followed by retry. Lost IPA replies and interruption while the gateway journal is pending are exercised by helper fault models, not by native packet-loss/process-kill injection.
- The complete CLI output contains the actionable unknown-ownership message. Persisted formal `Blocker.Detail` may retain only a generic Ansible failure when stderr contains a warning; this record does not claim actionable JSON-only diagnostics.
- The ambient controller closure has unresolved nested lookup/external-input dependencies. This is exact-candidate evidence with all native arms rerun; no source/base-change reuse is claimed. Independent review additionally matched the executed lifecycle helper to the candidate blob: SHA-256 `f20dc45b593246fa133dfeb808f02babcd3f5c63413701470be6b499dffae1c9`.
